updates.name: Samuel Truett
updates.bio: Professor of history at the University of New Mexico and director of its Center for the Southwest. A borderlands historian, he also works on environmental, Indigenous, Mexican and transnational history and the North American West; newer projects trace Indigenous and trans-imperial connections reaching Europe, the Indian Ocean and the Pacific. Author of Fugitive Landscapes (Yale, 2006).
updates.research_interests: borderlands history; environmental history; history of the North American West; nineteenth-century Mexico; Native American and Indigenous history; transnational history; empires and borderlands in world history

updates.name: Sang M. Han
updates.bio: Regents' Professor of chemical and biological engineering at the University of New Mexico, also appointed in electrical and computer engineering, with a PhD from UC Santa Barbara and a BS from UC Berkeley. His research covers germanium quantum structures and films grown on silicon, III-V integration on Ge-on-Si substrates, micro/nanofluidic bioseparation, semiconductor surface chemistry and nanocrystal synthesis.
updates.research_interests: selective growth of Ge quantum structures and heteroepitaxial films on Si; III-V integration on Ge-on-Si substrates for photovoltaics, electronics and sensors; micro/nanofluidic bioseparation and analysis; semiconductor surface modification; nanocrystal synthesis and functionalization

updates.name: Sebastian Medina
updates.bio: Pharmaceutical sciences faculty member in the UNM College of Pharmacy who studies how environmental metals harm human health, especially how arsenic compounds damage blood-forming stem and progenitor cells and how metals and other toxicants disrupt immune function, linking basic laboratory findings with human-based studies.
updates.research_interests: metal-induced hematotoxicity; inorganic and organic arsenicals; immune dysfunction from toxicant exposure; genotoxicity

updates.name: Thomas De Pree
updates.bio: Environmental anthropologist with a science and technology studies PhD from Rensselaer, holding research faculty status at UNM and teaching at Southwestern Indian Polytechnic Institute. Research grew from community work in the former Grants uranium mining district on contested mine cleanup, and now, in the UNM METALS Community Engagement Core, brings Indigenous knowledge into studies of abandoned uranium mine exposures.
updates.research_interests: environmental anthropology; science and technology studies; political ecology; environmental health sciences; abandoned uranium mine remediation; community-engaged research

updates.name: Thomas Turner
updates.bio: Regents' Professor and Curator of Fishes at the University of New Mexico, leading the Turner Aquatic Conservation Lab. Research covers the evolution and ecology of aquatic species and communities using stable isotopes, genomics, museum collections and experiments, plus science and policy for endangered species; also co-chairs an independent review panel for the Columbia Basin fish and wildlife program.
updates.research_interests: evolution and ecology of aquatic species, populations and communities; life history variation; disturbance, climate and land-use change; phylogenetic and geological history of biodiversity; endangered species science and policy

updates.name: Lowell W. Fritz
updates.bio: Researcher at the Seattle-based Alaska Fisheries Science Center of NOAA Fisheries whose Steller sea lion work, begun in 1990, centred on population dynamics, demography and interactions with commercial fisheries; he also studied prey fishes such as Atka mackerel, walleye pollock and Pacific cod. His career began at Rutgers' Haskin Shellfish Research Laboratory, studying mollusc shells.
updates.research_interests: Steller sea lion population dynamics and demographics; sea lion-fishery interactions; sea lion prey fishes
